result.summary: Removes the `private:` access specifiers from dummy STL node helper structs in `src/memusage.h`. These structs exist solely to approximate container node sizes using `sizeof` for dynamic memory estimation.
result.problem: Clang 24 diagnoses unused private fields in `stl_tree_node`, `list_node`, and `unordered_node` with `-Wunused-private-field`, generating compiler warnings across multiple translation units because the helper fields are never accessed.
evidence: Compiler build output provided in the PR description showing multiple `-Wunused-private-field` warnings generated across several translation units (`logging.cpp`, `txmempool.cpp`, `txgraph.cpp`, tests).
Author cites upstream change llvm/llvm-project#237374 introducing the warning in Clang 24.
result.changed_since_previous: No changes to the patch content or commit.
result.card: This pull request removes three private access specifiers from STL container layout helper structs in src/memusage.h. These dummy structs exist solely to approximate container node sizes for dynamic memory estimation, and their fields are never accessed. Clang 24 warns on them with -Wunused-private-field, cluttering compiler output or failing warning-as-error builds. Making the fields public silences the warning without changing struct sizes or memory calculations.

risk.why: Only changes access specifiers on dummy structs used exclusively for sizeof calculations in memory usage tracking.
